archetype.name: Pocket Passer (veteran timing thrower)
archetype.definition: A 38-year-old, 18th-year pocket quarterback who wins from a clean platform with anticipation and intermediate accuracy rather than his legs, and whose game this year has shrunk toward the short and middle levels.

report.headline: Leads the league in yards, but the deep ball has gone missing
report.take:
Stafford is the same quarterback he has been in McVay's system: a pocket thrower who gets rid of it on time, takes few sacks and lives on rhythm throws to the sideline and over the linebackers. The volume says star. He is first in passing yards and on a 4,830-yard pace. The efficiency says something closer to the middle of the league: 0.12 EPA per dropback ranks 18th of 45, after a 2025 in which he led the league in yards and touchdowns at 0.228 EPA per play. The yards come from 39.7 attempts a game in an offense that passes more than the situation calls for (fifth in pass rate over expected), not from unusual efficiency per throw.

The engine is the 10-19 yard window. Those 61 throws produced 0.475 EPA apiece and 29.0 EPA in total, which is more than his whole dropback EPA total of 26.1. That means everything else, taken together, has given points back. Davante Adams is the main beneficiary at 0.451 EPA per target, well ahead of Puka Nacua's 0.189 on more volume. The protection has helped too. He has been pressured on just 14.9% of dropbacks, sixth-lowest, and sacked on 3.8%. The short game is clean as well, with 78.5% completions and a +5 CPOE under 10 air yards.

The numbers hide two things. First, the deep ball has collapsed: 24.1% completions and three interceptions on 29 throws of 20-plus yards, with a CPOE of -12.8. That is a small sample, and at his age it is the split that will get the most scrutiny. Second, the offense seems to have responded by taking the deep ball off the table. His aggressiveness is down 4.9 points from last year, and his intended air yards fell to 4.8 and 4.9 in Weeks 6 and 7. The completion rate (75.9% over the last three) and the interception rate (0.9%) look much better for it. Yards per attempt has not followed, and his third-down EPA is negative because he is throwing short of the sticks.

The 2025 aggressiveness of 19.3 was actually the outlier. His Rams seasons from 2021 to 2024 sat around 12-13, so this year's 14.39 is a return to his norm rather than a cliff. The interceptions are also part of his career profile, not a new problem. Where this goes depends on whether the short-and-intermediate version can keep stacking efficient games without the deep shots. If it can, he settles in as a high-volume, above-average starter. If the deep game never returns, expect more weeks like Week 6, when the Rams scored 16 points as 12.5-point favorites.

strengths.title: Intermediate window drives the offense
strengths.body: Throws of 10-19 yards have been the best part of his game: hugely efficient and responsible for more EPA than his season total. That is timing and anticipation over the middle and outside the numbers, and Adams has been the main outlet. It is sustainable because it is the core of how he has always played in this scheme, though the per-throw rate on 61 attempts will likely cool somewhat.

strengths.title: Cleaner ball placement than ever charted
strengths.body: His bad-throw rate of 12.9% is 4.5 points better than last year and the best of any season with charting in his career, where he usually ran 16-20%. Part of that is the shorter menu, since easier throws are easier to place. The last three games pushed CPOE to 4.3. The accuracy is real, but it is tied to the conservative throw selection.

strengths.title: Avoids pressure and sacks
strengths.body: He is rarely pressured and rarely sacked, with both rates among the best in the league. Behind that are a timing offense, a quick-enough release (2.73 seconds) and a line that has held up. His 2024-25 pressure-to-sack rates were also strong, so this is a trait rather than luck.

concerns.title: Deep passing has fallen apart
concerns.body: On 20-plus-yard throws he is completing a quarter of his attempts, 12.8 points below expectation, with three interceptions. Twenty-nine attempts is a hint rather than proof, and last year he pushed the ball downfield successfully. Still, the staff's move to an intended air distance under 5 yards in the last two games suggests they see it too. Whether that reflects arm strength at 38 or a bad run of throws is the biggest open question of his season.

concerns.title: Turnovers remain part of the package
concerns.body: Seven interceptions ranks 41st of 45 and puts him on a 17-interception pace. Three came deep and four came to the right side. This is long-standing for him: he threw 17 in 2021 while ranking near the bottom of the league. The last-three interception rate of 0.9% is the best sign, but it came with the conservative approach, so it is not clear it survives if he starts pushing the ball again.

concerns.title: Volume outruns efficiency
concerns.body: First in yards but 18th in EPA per dropback: the counting stats are inflated by attempts. Third down shows the cost of the shorter approach. He is facing 7.5 yards to go on average, throwing just short of the sticks, and losing EPA there. Unless the downfield element returns, the gap between the yardage rank and the efficiency rank should persist.

trend.note: His game EPA has swung from -5.6 to 18.6 and back, with big efficiency games against the Giants and Bills and flat or negative outings against Denver, Philadelphia and Arizona. Over the last three games he has been more efficient and more careful, but in the last two the yardage dropped as the throws got shorter.

nextGame.headline: Stingy underneath, leaky deep, and a script that caps volume
nextGame.body:
The Chargers are the wrong defense for the version of Stafford from the last two weeks. They are ninth in short-pass EPA and seventh against the pass overall, and they allow the seventh-fewest fantasy points to quarterbacks. Their weakness is deep, where they rank 24th, which is exactly the area he has struggled with. They also hit quarterbacks at the fifth-highest rate, a real test for a line that has kept him clean. Their offense is the worst in the league by EPA and the most run-leaning, and the Rams are 6.5-point home favorites. If the game goes to form, Stafford may be throwing with a lead and fewer attempts. His efficiency when up by 9 or more (0.166 EPA per play) has been fine, but the volume would shrink.

On availability, Derwin James (94% of snaps) is listed questionable with a hamstring, as are corners Donte Jackson and Rodney Shelley. Those reports date to October 20, so treat them as stale. If James sits, the middle and deep areas get softer, and that is where Stafford wins with Adams. On the Chargers' offense, tackle Joe Alt, Ladd McConkey and Tre' Harris are all questionable, which could make their offense even less able to keep pace and keep the Rams throwing. On his own side, only reserve tight end Terrance Ferguson is out, and Higbee and Parkinson have been covering that role all season. The game is indoors.

keyMatchups.title: Deep shots against a soft shell
keyMatchups.body: The Chargers give up a lot on deep passes, and Stafford's deep game has been his worst split all year. This is the best chance yet to see whether he and the staff will keep testing downfield or keep it short against a defense built to stop short throws. One or two connections deep would change his line considerably.

keyMatchups.title: Adams against a soft WR2 profile
keyMatchups.body: Los Angeles has held opposing top receivers well under their averages (fourth-best) but has let second receivers outscore theirs (31st). With Nacua leading the target count, Adams fits the WR2 role, and he has been Stafford's most efficient target. Early-season role ranks depend partly on who the Chargers have faced, but the lean points toward Adams.

keyMatchups.title: Game script from a broken offense
keyMatchups.body: The Chargers rank last in offensive EPA and last in pass rate over expected. That points to a low-event game the Rams should control, with Stafford's attempts trimmed in the second half. A 44.5 total says the Book sees the same thing.

nextGame.watch: Whether he throws anything 20-plus yards early against a secondary that may be missing Derwin James. That will tell us whether the recent short-only approach is a game plan or a ceiling.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect the volume to stay high and the efficiency to sit above league average but short of 2025. The pass-first tilt, the protection and the intermediate timing game are all stable, so something in the range of 250-290 passing yards a game is reasonable even with a few game scripts like this week's. The touchdown rate has room to hold given his red-zone production (12 touchdowns on 40 attempts) and an offense that ranks fourth in success rate, so 1.6-2.2 a game fits.

What regresses: the intermediate EPA rate is very high and will probably come down some, and the recent 0.9% interception rate is unlikely to last over his career baseline, so plan on 0.6-1.0 interceptions a game. What could rebound: a deep game that has been historically bad on just 29 throws. Even a move back toward ordinary there would lift his yards per attempt and EPA, which is where the upside in this projection lives. If the deep ball really is gone, he is a high-volume, middle-of-the-pack efficiency passer the rest of the way.
swingFactors: Whether the deep ball returns or stays off the menu
Pass protection holding at its current low-pressure level
Adams staying healthy as the most efficient target

confidence.note: Seven games with a clear pocket profile, but the deep split rests on 29 throws and the approach changed in the last two games.
